sanskrit: skambheneme viṣkabhite dyauś ca bhūmiś ca tiṣṭhataḥ | skambha idaṃ sarvam ārpitam ejad yat prāṇan nimiṣac ca yat ||
english: By the Skambha are these two propped and held apart — heaven and earth stand firm. In the Skambha all this is established: whatever stirs, whatever breathes and blinks.

sanskrit: ekacakraṃ vartata ekanemi sahasrākṣaraṃ pra puro ni paścāt | ardhenedaṃ pari babhūva viśvaṃ yad asyārdhaṃ katamaḥ sa ketuḥ ||
english: Single-wheeled it revolves, single-rimmed, with a thousand syllables — forward it moves and backward. With half of itself it has encompassed all this universe; as for the other half, what is that emblem?

sanskrit: pañcavāhi vahaty agram asya pṛṣṭayo yuktā anusaṃvahanti | ayātam asya dadṛśe na yātaṃ paraṃ nedīyo 'varaṃ davīyaḥ ||
english: A five-coursed team draws its van; the flanks, yoked, haul in sequence. Its yet-untraveled course cannot be seen, nor its traveled one — what is far is nearer, what is near is more remote.

sanskrit: idaṃ savitar vi jānīhi ṣaḍ yamā eka ekajaḥ | tasmin hāpitvam icchante ya eṣām eka ekajaḥ ||
english: Know this, O Savitṛ: six paired ones and one that is born singly. In him do they seek communion — he who among them is born as one.

sanskrit: tiryagbilaś camasa ūrdhvabudhno yasmin yaśo nihitaṃ viśvarūpam | atrāsata ṛṣayaḥ sapta sākaṃ ye asya gopā mahato babhūvuḥ ||
english: A cup whose opening faces sideways and whose base is upward — in it is laid the glory of all forms. Here together sat the seven seers who became the guardians of this great one.

sanskrit: tisro ha prajā atyāyam āyan ny anyā arkam abhito +'viśanta | bṛhan ha tasthau rajaso vimāno harito hariṇīr ā viveśa ||
english: Three creatures passed across the crossing; others poured inward around the sun. The great one stood as measurer of the atmosphere; into the tawny mares the golden one entered.

sanskrit: dvādaśa pradhayaś cakram ekaṃ trīṇi nabhyāni ka u tac ciketa | tatrāhatās trīṇi śatāni śaṅkavaḥ ṣaṣṭiś ca khīlā avicācalā ye ||
english: Twelve fellies, one wheel, three hubs — who has perceived this? In it are fixed three hundred and sixty pegs and sixty more — immovable they stand.

sanskrit: anantaṃ vitataṃ purutrā anantam antavac cā samakte | te nākapālaś carati prajānan vidvān bhūtaṃ yad u bhavyam asya ||
english: Infinite and spread across many places — the infinite and the finite meet face to face. The guardian of the vault of heaven moves knowing both: he who is wise knows what has come to be and what shall yet come to be.

sanskrit: āviḥ san nihitaṃ guhā jaran nāma mahat padam | tatraidaṃ sarvam ārpitam ejat prāṇan nimiṣac ca yat ||
english: Manifest yet concealed in the cave — ancient is the name, great is the station. In that is all this established: whatever stirs, whatever breathes and blinks.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ bharantam udakaṃ kumbhenevodahāryam | paśyanti sarve cakṣuṣā na sarve manasā viduḥ ||
english: Bearing water upward, as if a water-vessel fit to be carried — all behold it with the eye; not all know it with the mind.

sanskrit: ūnāt pūrṇam ud acati pūrṇād ūnam ud acyate | kaviṣ ṭad brahmā veda yatas tat pariṣicyate ||
english: From the deficient the full arises; from the full the deficient is drawn forth. The seer, the brahman, knows from whence it is poured around.

sanskrit: prajāpatiś carati garbhe antar adṛśyamāno bahudhā pra jāyate | ardhena viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ jajāna yad asyārdhaṃ kim u taj jajāna ||
english: Prajāpati moves within the womb, unseen; in manifold ways he is born. With half of himself he engendered the whole world of beings — as for the other half, what did that bring forth?

sanskrit: yad ejati carati yac ca tiṣṭhaty aprāṇat prāṇan nimiṣac ca tiṣṭhat | tad dādhāra pṛthivīṃ viśvarūpaṃ tat saṃbhūya bhavaty ekam eva ||
english: What stirs and moves and what stands still — the breathless breathing, the blinking yet at rest — that of all forms has sustained the earth; coming together, it becomes one alone.

sanskrit: yā purastād yujyate yota paścād yā viśvato yujyate yota sarvataḥ | yayā yajñas tāyate prāṅ tāṃ tvā pṛcchāmi katamā nu sarcām ||
english: She who is yoked in front and likewise behind, she who is yoked on all sides and in every direction — she by whom the sacrifice is stretched forth toward the east: of her I ask you — which of these strands is she?

sanskrit: yataḥ sūrya udety astaṃ yatra ca gacchati | tad eva manye 'haṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ tato nāpy eti kiṃ cana ||
english: Whence the sun rises and where it sets — that alone I hold to be the highest; from that nothing whatsoever goes beyond.

sanskrit: satyenordhvas tapati brahmaṇā- -arvāṅ vi paśyati | prāṇena tiryaṅ prāṇati yasmin jyeṣṭham adhi śritam ||
english: By truth it blazes upward; by brahman it looks downward; by breath it breathes laterally — upon this the highest is established.

sanskrit: yo vai te vidyād araṇī yābhyāṃ nirmathyate vasu | sa vidvān jyeṣṭhaṃ manyeta sa vidyād brāhmaṇaṃ mahat ||
english: He who would know those two fire-sticks from which wealth is churned forth — that knowing one would esteem the highest; he would know the great brahman.

sanskrit: apād agre sam abhavat so agre svar ābharat | catuṣpād bhūtvā bhogyaḥ sarvam ādatta bhojanam ||
english: Footless at first it came into being; at first it brought the sun forth. Having become four-footed and worthy of enjoyment, it took all nourishment.

sanskrit: bhogyo bhavad atho annam adad bahu | yo devam uttarāvantam upāsātai sanātanam ||
english: It became worthy of enjoyment and thereafter consumed abundant food — he who worships the eternal god possessed of exaltation.

sanskrit: sanātanam enam āhur utādyāsat punar navaḥ | ahorātre pra jāyete anyo anyasya rūpayoḥ ||
english: They call him eternal, yet today he shines again as new. Day and night are born in turn, each taking the form of the other.

sanskrit: śataṃ sahasram ayutaṃ nyarbudam asaṃkhyeyaṃ svam asmin niviṣṭam | tad asya ghnanty abhipaśyata eva tasmād devo rocate sa etat ||
english: A hundred, a thousand, ten thousand, a billion — the incalculable treasure lodged within this: they smite it only while they look on it. Therefore the god shines; it is he.

sanskrit: ārāgramātraṃ dadṛśa utaikaṃ naiva dṛśyate | tataḥ pariṣvajīyasī devatā sā mama priyā ||
english: No more than the tip of an awl has it been seen — and yet it is not seen at all. More embracing than all that is this deity; she is my beloved.

sanskrit: iyaṃ kalyāṇy ajarā martyasyāmṛtā gṛhe | yasmai kṛtā śaye sa yaś cakāra tadāra saḥ ||
english: This auspicious one, unaging and immortal, dwells in the house of the mortal. He for whom she was made lies with her; he who fashioned her has reached that goal.

sanskrit: tvaṃ strī tvaṃ pumān asi tvaṃ kumāry uta vā kumāraḥ | tvaṃ jīrṇo daṇḍena vañcasi tvaṃ jāto bhavasi viśvatomukhaḥ ||
english: You are woman, you are man; you are the maiden and the boy. You, grown old, totter with a staff; you, once born, become the one whose face is everywhere.

sanskrit: utaiṣa jyeṣṭha uta vā kaniṣṭha utaiṣa bhrātota vā pitaiṣaḥ | eko devo manasi praviṣṭaḥ prathamo jātaḥ sa u garbhe antaḥ ||
english: And this one is the eldest, and likewise the youngest; this one is the brother and also the father. The one god who has entered the mind — first-born is he, yet even now he is within the womb.

sanskrit: anejaty ejati sarvam asmin viśvā bhūtāni paryābhṛtasya | sa pumān puṃso janayann ṛtena sarvān antān gacchatu tiṣṭhann eva ||
english: Without stirring he sets all this in motion; all beings are borne around within him who bears all. That male, engendering from the male by cosmic law — standing firm, let him reach all ends.

sanskrit: madhye divo nihitaḥ pṛśniraśmā vi cakramāṇau rajasasphātyantau | sa viśvābhir abhi caṣṭe śacībhir antarā pūrvam aparaṃ ca ketum ||
english: Set in the midst of heaven, the speckled stone — and these two striding ones cleave the atmosphere asunder. He surveys all with his powers, between the eastern and the western light.

sanskrit: ye arvāg uta vā purāṇe vedaṃ vidvāṃsam abhito vadanti | ādityam eva te pari vadanti sarve agniṃ dvitīyaṃ trivṛtaṃ ca haṃsam ||
english: Those who speak on all sides of the knower of the Veda — whether of recent times or of ancient — all of them are speaking of Āditya alone, of Agni the second, and the triple-woven haṃsa.

sanskrit: ekām ṛcaṃ sam indhate dvādaśabhir agnibhiḥ | tasyām āpas tasyāṃ gāvas tasyām oṣadhayaḥ śritāḥ ||
english: A single ṛc they kindle with twelve fires. In it the waters are established, in it the cattle, in it the plants take refuge.

sanskrit: sapta suparṇā upa dhamanta bāṇam anuṣṭubhā saṃbhṛtaṃ vāyum etam | tam ātataṃ vitataṃ tantum ātataṃ manaḥ punātu salilasya pṛṣṭhe ||
english: Seven fair-winged ones blow upon the arrow, this wind gathered in the anuṣṭubh. Let the mind purify that stretched-out thread, stretched and spread upon the surface of the water.

sanskrit: sapta ṛṣayaḥ pratihitāḥ śarīre sapta rakṣanti sadam apramādam | saptāpaḥ svapato lokam īyus tatra jāgṛto asvapnajau satrasadau ca devau ||
english: Seven seers are set within the body; seven guard it always without fail. Seven waters went to the world of one who sleeps — there the two gods who do not sleep, who arose from wakefulness, sat together at the sattra.
